resources.string: Draws a trusted, fully opaque overlay showing an inverted copy of the app in front, while pen and touch pass straight through to it. Needs accessibility because only a trusted overlay may be opaque and non-touchable at the same time, and because window screenshots are the only capture on this device that cannot capture the overlay itself.
The overlay is opaque, so it hides itself while you are in this app and comes back when you leave. Pen and touch always pass through to the app underneath.

BOOX auto-freeze disables sideloaded apps after a couple of minutes in the background. Freezing Inkverse kills the overlay — the screen goes back to light — and also drops it from the Accessibility list, which is why it has to be enabled again by hand every time. Exclude Inkverse from auto-freeze in the BOOX app manager (long-press the app, turn off auto-freeze / add it to the whitelist) and both stop happening.
Accessibility service is off.\nEnable “Inkverse” in Accessibility settings — that is what allows a fully opaque overlay that still lets touch through.

Inkverse was inverting, and its accessibility service is gone.\nNothing turned it off: BOOX auto-freeze disabled the app, which also removes it from the Accessibility list. Enable it again below, then exclude Inkverse from auto-freeze so it stops happening.
Running. Leave this app and the inverted view appears.
Confirm the install when the system asks.
